claims.explanation: Teniposide is a topoisomerase II poison whose cytotoxicity depends on TOP2A/TOP2B expression and on intact DNA-damage/apoptosis signaling; selective killing therefore tracks with high TOP2A expression and functional p53-dependent or p53-independent apoptotic responses, while efflux pumps (ABCB1, MRP3/ABCC3) and low proliferative/topoisomerase activity protect. The virtual-cell signature (TOP2A down, GADD45A/EGR1/NF-kB up) and the topoisomerase-inhibitor similarity confirm on-target TOP2 engagement, and the resistant lines are enriched for low-proliferation or efflux-capable contexts.

features.basis: primary drug target; higher TOP2A gives more drug-stabilized cleavage complexes
epipodophyllotoxin efflux lowers intracellular teniposide
MRP3 transports epipodophyllotoxins and confers resistance
p53-mutant tumors often retain high proliferation and DNA-damage sensitivity; many killed lines are TP53-mutant
loss of p16/CDKN2A releases proliferation and increases TOP2-dependent killing
virtual-cell upregulation indicates intact DNA-damage response after teniposide
NF-kB/AP-1 activation drives FasL-dependent apoptosis after teniposide
FasL induction mediates DNA-damage-induced apoptosis in lymphocytes
second topoisomerase II isoform also targeted by teniposide
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006) are among least affected, suggesting survival signaling blunts damage response
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines SH4/UACC62 split response, but BRAF-driven MAPK survival may reduce sensitivity
ATM loss impairs DNA-damage repair and can increase topoisomerase-poison cytotoxicity
